A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Graph-R1 and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their content can be reliably matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and cross-dataset generalization experiments in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds mixed-training and specialized-domain results in Appendix K. Its Graph-R1 and Search-R1 results are distinguished from the externally sourced GPT-4o-mini baseline scores.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the multi-turn policy, dual entity/hyperedge retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion, and GRPO with format/F1 rewards. Appendix J expands construction documentation without establishing a revised Graph-R1 procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains the six original QA benchmarks and adds zero-shot evaluation on Medicine, Agriculture, CS, Legal, and Mix datasets in Appendix K.2. These substantially broaden the evaluated domains.

E2.justification: The main comparator membership is unchanged. Added experiments reuse Search-R1 and the existing GPT-4o-mini comparator set; Table 6 explicitly imports the latter's scores from HyperGraphRAG. Newly cited graph methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V1 Table 5 specifies three epochs for R1, Search-R1, R1-Searcher, and Graph-R1; v2 Table 3 specifies one. Appendix K adds combined-dataset training with controlled total data volume and specialized-domain zero-shot testing. These substantially extend the protocols; the unchanged main scores do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing ablations, sensitivity comparisons, case study, and transfer heatmaps remain. Appendix K adds a controlled comparison of dataset-specific, single-source transfer, and mixed-dataset training, plus specialized-domain transfer tests, substantially extending the generalization analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional tables continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original transfer heatmaps retain their numerical results. V2 adds substantial result sets: combined-training average F1 is 48.19 for Graph-R1 versus 35.25 for Search-R1, and specialized-domain average F1 is 39.26 versus 24.32. These concern newly reported conditions, not same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains the three propositions and their mathematical arguments, and Appendix C retains the complexity analysis. Equation consolidation, renumbering, and shortening the standard F1 explanation do not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contribution and claims about accuracy, retrieval efficiency, and generation quality remain. V2's abstract emphasizes being the first such framework, but v1 already makes that novelty claim in Section 2. Generalization claims remain in the relocated and expanded appendix discussion.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1 Appendix H's explicit limitations concerning construction cost, missing structural reasoning in retrieval, and text-only knowledge. Appendix K adds interpretations about transferable relational biases and the benefits of domain-aligned versus mixed supervision. Together these materially change the discussion of applicability and limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix J newly specifies 1200-token chunks with 50-token overlap and explains the construction and vector-storage pipeline. The abstract extends the availability statement from code to software and data, and Appendix G revises the epoch setting. Conversely, Section 4 omits v1's explicit answer-reward tokenization preprocessing note.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds works including G-Reasoner, Youtu-GraphRAG, and GraphSearch, while removing examples such as VLM-R1 and ZeroSearch. The overall research positioning remains similar; numerous other bibliography edits are publication updates to retained works.

P1.justification: V2 condenses wording and subsection titles, moves the case study and generalization section into Appendices H–I, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. V2 combines the cost table and generation radar chart into Figure 6, relocates existing displays, and adds Figure 12 and experimental Tables 5–6. Relocated Figure 11 also replaces informative method/metric subcaptions with misleading generic labels.

improvement.justification: The controlled mixed-training comparison and specialized-domain transfer tests provide useful additional evidence beyond v1's cross-validation among six QA benchmarks. Appendix J also improves construction reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the removal of explicit limitations and misleading labels in the relocated generalization figure, making the overall improvement limited.
